usage.callShape: POST https://stableupload.dev/api/site with JSON body {filename, tier}
usage.outputShape: body.uploadId, body.uploadMethod ("post"|"put"), body.postUrl + body.postFields (S3 multipart fields) for POST, or body.uploadUrl for PUT, body.curlExample (ready-to-run upload command), body.expiresAt, body.maxSize, body.uploadUrlExpiresAt. NOTE: /api/site does NOT return body.publicUrl in the immediate response (unlike /api/upload) — the served site URL is obtained after the zip is uploaded and activated.
quirks: This is the SITE endpoint (zip -> static site hosting), distinct from /api/upload (single file). Body is {filename, tier} with NO contentType field (the API forces Content-Type application/zip for the upload).

PRICE IS TIER-DEPENDENT. The default x402 quote is $2.00 (= '1gb' tier) but the body's 'tier' field overrides the charge. Site tiers: 10mb=$0.02, 100mb=$0.20, 1gb=$2.00, short-10mb=$0.005, short-100mb=$0.02, short-1gb=$0.10. short-5gb is NOT supported for sites. Pick the smallest that fits to minimize cost (tested short-10mb = $0.005).

TWO-STEP FLOW: POST /api/site only ISSUES a presigned S3 form — it does NOT accept file bytes. Second step: POST the zip to body.postUrl as multipart/form-data including every key/value in body.postFields PLUS a 'file' part with the zip bytes (body.curlExample is the exact command). Verified the S3 upload returns HTTP 204 on success.
Unlike /api/upload, the /api/site response does NOT include publicUrl. The static-site URL is resolved after the zip is uploaded (and activated/extracted).
Presigned form expires fast (uploadUrlExpiresAt ~15 min) — upload promptly. Site retention: expiresAt is 7 days for short-* tiers, 6 months for default tiers.
txHash field in the qa-pay response was null on this call (paid:true, confirmed:false), but payment settled and the call returned 200.
usage.guide: Call POST https://stableupload.dev/api/site with JSON {filename, tier} to host a static site from a zip. Use the smallest tier that fits (short-10mb ~ $0.005 for <10MB; the registry's $2 surface is the 1gb tier). The 'tier' field sets the actual charge even though the unpaid quote shows $2.00. The response is a presigned S3 upload ticket, NOT a stored site. Second step: actually upload the zip — POST it as multipart/form-data to body.postUrl, including all body.postFields plus a 'file' part with the zip bytes (body.curlExample is a ready-to-run command); a 204 means success. After upload the bundle is served as a static site (resolve the URL post-activation). No auth/API key; payment is per call via x402.
